rationale: Recording the outcome of the repeat execution of the experiment that carries the main finding: it reproduced every comparison with the same outcomes and witness indices, so the account is schedule-stable rather than a product of one interleaving. I fold that into the main question's current account instead of opening a new question, since a repeat can only strengthen or weaken the existing explanation.

interpretations.rationale: Current account across six receipts, one of which is a repeat that reproduced the same experiment identically. A MsgForgetLeader in peer wire form (From=3, To=2, no term field) is accepted with no error through both documented inbound paths - RawNode.Step (index 4 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7, reproduced at 22 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a) and the real Node interface that applications use, where the node's own reported leader went 1 -> 0 and the same transition was produced by the intended local API Node.ForgetLeader (indices 42 and 43 of CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40, with the local-type control holding at 41). It changes the support a follower gives a log-up-to-date candidate: the identical pre-vote that produced no response under the lease is granted after the accepted message, the follower then grants the real vote, and the candidate becomes StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent still reports StateLeader at term 2 (indices 14, 15 and 17 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; index 25 of the latest). The window per message is closed by the next genuine leader message (heartbeat restored lead=1 after one leader tick, index 7, and the same pre-vote was ignored again, index 8), but a sender repeating the message each round keeps it open without any repair failing: three consecutive rounds restored the context and granted again (indices 32, 35, 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849, whose repair comparisons hold at 33 and 36). The harm stays bounded: after the forged election the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append, becomes a follower at term 3 following it, and the anchor equals the committed prefix it already had (index 26 of CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a), so no committed entry was lost. Cause and controls are unchanged: MsgForgetLeader is absent from isLocalMsg although only the local ForgetLeader APIs produce it, and because the wire form carries no term field Step treats it as a local message and skips term checks; a genuinely local type from the same sender is still rejected or ignored in every receipt. Conditions the effect depends on, stated explicitly: the defeated lease test exists only when Config.CheckQuorum is set (inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout), so the marginal effect of the forged message is specific to CheckQuorum deployments; the type is a no-op on leaders, so the incumbent keeps serving until it learns a higher term; and a candidate whose log is behind is still refused by isUpToDate, so the message does not manufacture support for stale candidates. The exposure this creates is now measured rather than only bounded by reading: an elected leader that afterwards hears from nobody is already a follower at its first CheckQuorum check, with its term unchanged, and stays a follower at the next sample (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512), so the overlap between the incumbent and the forged leader lasts one election timeout of the incumbent's own clock in the silent case. Remaining limits are scope: single process, hand-delivered messages, one tick configuration, ReadOnlyLeaseBased refusing the message outright, and the persistence loop using an exact one-message-per-tick cadence. The repeat of this very experiment from its retained inputs in a clean copy returned the same twelve comparison outcomes with the same witness indices (under-lease controls holding at 3, 4, 7 and 10; the peer-form message accepted at 5 and 13; the same pre-vote granted afterwards at 6 and 14; the vote granted at 15; the candidate leading at term 3 at 17; the repair heartbeat and the ignored pre-vote after it at 7 and 8), which is what makes the account schedule-stable rather than the product of one favourable interleaving.
counterevidence: The competing explanation that followers grant pre-votes and votes regardless of their leader is excluded by the under-lease control in every receipt, including the control round inside the persistence loop and the Node-interface control.
The change is per-message and reversible: the context returns with the next real leader heartbeat in every round, so this is not a stuck state and does not survive a sender that stops.
The widest severity reading is excluded by the aftermath receipt: the deposed incumbent conceded and the new leader's log continued the committed prefix, so no committed entry was lost.
ReadOnlyLeaseBased still refuses MsgForgetLeader in stepFollower, so lease-based reads are not broken by this mechanism.
limitations: Fault-model assumption: a peer may deliver a protobuf message of any type - including one the module only produces locally - to the documented inbound path, repeatedly; the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the protection under test.

Single-process, hand-delivered messages: no wall-clock duration, jitter, packet loss, authentication or multi-host transport behaviour is measured, and the persistence loop used an exact one-message-per-tick cadence.
The quorum-scale election was measured on one voter plus the candidate in the earlier receipt and not re-measured under the repeated cadence.

The incumbent's overlap with the new leader is bounded and measured for the silent case - one election timeout of its own clock with an unchanged term (indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512) - but that bound does not follow when the leader still hears from some voters, or when CheckQuorum is disabled.
The effect requires CheckQuorum to be enabled for the lease test it defeats, and it is a follower-side change only (leaders ignore the type).

Reproduction: this experiment was executed twice from its fixed inputs in clean copies and both runs produced identical comparison outcomes and witness indices, so the observations are not an artefact of one scheduling; the earlier repeat of the parent harness is not claimed to extend to the later probes of this run, which were each executed once.
interpretations.joint_history: All five cited receipts are separate executions of one fixed-experiment lineage in the same package with the same construction: three real RawNode instances (plus, in the last one, a real Node started by RestartNode) built from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1 with voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, a real election for node 1 and messages delivered through the public Step path. CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 is the original harness; CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568 is its revised successor (previous_id = the original) adding the repair-path and quorum scenarios; CheckRun ab6a2e0bcad44cc9beea9c847694939a adds the aftermath scenario with per-stream event names; CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849 adds the per-round persistence loop; CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40 adds the real Node interface scenario. Each run builds its own instances and prints into its own runner stream, so no cited index depends on another run's bytes; where the same predicate is witnessed in several receipts it is because the harness re-executed the scenario, never because observations were joined across runs. CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512 adds the six-in-process scenario that measures the incumbent's own quorum check; it reuses the same construction and the election helper, so its indices 45-46 are read from that run's own stream and not joined with any other.
